questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore spain outside the bigger cities and the most common tourist destinations.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: there were a lot of practical stuff that spoiled the experience with concerns

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: it felt like all the information you needed wasn't easy to find, and you would be lucky if you or one of your friends stumpled apon it, before it was too late.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: there weren't any information beside the introduction day for the Erasmus students. when I tried to reach out to the coordinators at UAL, they never replied or replied multiple weeks after my request, they never ended helping me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: the introduction day gave me the impression that they were a good host university, but after that day, there were no help to be found.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used spotahome, it felt save and I didn't have any problems with it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I was a little late looking for house, so I would recommend future students too find a place at least a couple of months before. you could also join the whatsapp group chat, tough link on instagram, and ask someone if they know a place available for rent.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: nice areas, reasonable prices, but the majority of the options didn't have an ac

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: a lot af different processes had to align to make sure it all went smoothly, I didnt for me, so I had a lot of issues with the registration. it was very stressfull to not be registered properly 2 weeks before leaving for exchange. I had to call the office before I was taken serious and it was fixed.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: the same as above

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: the only way to get help if you are lucky you call the right office. they never answer emails

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to get the ones I wanted, but it was a very complicated process to choose the classes and even more to change them again, it is possible though.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: make sure your classes don't overlap, its very hard to find 5 classes that don't, but you need to, to be able to pass.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very limited options for classes, and overall I didn't like the way of teaching and the way the exams were held.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the level was what a would consider below BA level at my home university, but the way the classes and exams where performed, made it unnecessary hard to pass the classes in the end.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: the one at my home university is very free and mostly depend on the exam in the end, while at my host university its a mix of your attendance, participation during classes and the exam. the way of teaching is very different too, where its mostly based on facts you have to recall facts at the exam. the teachers are also a lot more strict in my host university.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: The History and Culture of Hispanic Countries, Specialized uses of the Spanish Language, Global History of the Present, Foundations of General Linguistics, Interculturalism Policies in anglophone Countries

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I had a very nice experience with the teachers from the clases 'Interculturalism Policies in anglophone Countries' and 'Global History of the Present' the professors were very patient with exchange students and they were so nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the good options were hard to find, if you want more than just partying, since its a smaller city.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: a lot were planned by the organisation esn Almeria

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: all the activities in the introduction weeks, too meet a lot of new people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go on trips in the weekends, and experience the rest of Andalusia

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: in the beginning I had a hard time because everything was new and you get overwhelmed easily, when the weather gets better, it was a lot easier.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found it hard myself to mak local friends, since they mostly kept to themselves

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the way they act in public, everything is slow and they chat a lot in public, even with strangers

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I got used to the slower way of living, and ended up liking it a lot

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. mingle a lot in the beggining
2. explore the city and the region 
3. enjoy the beach

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: its not very serous at this university to get things done before a deadline, seemed like no one expected a deadline, so don't stress about that

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the people I meet and the things I learned about myself

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: creating a new life for myself, so far from home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
